data.gender_notes: Mirrikh is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The name Mirrikh is derived from the Arabic word 'mirrak', which translates to 'the night hunter'. It is a powerful and evocative name that evokes images of strength, courage, and wisdom in the face of the unknown. The name Mirrikh carries the meaning “The Night Hunter” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic. Parents who choose Mirrikh usually hope their child will grow to embody the night hunter and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Mirrikh is a name with deep spiritual significance in Islamic tradition. It is believed to represent the strength and courage of the night hunter, who fearlessly faces the darkness and brings light to the world. This name is also said to be a reminder of the power of the night, and the importance of remaining vigilant and alert in the face of adversity.

historical_references.reference: Mirrikh was a prominent figure during the Abbasid Caliphate (750-1258 CE) and is known for his contributions to Islamic scholarship, particularly in the field of hadith studies. He authored several important works and was a respected scholar in his time.

Another historical reference for Mirrikh comes from the period of the Mongol invasions (1221-1360 CE). Mirrikh served as a vizier for the Mongol ruler Hulagu Khan and played a crucial role in protecting Baghdad from complete destruction during the sack of the city. He also negotiated the release of prisoners and the payment of tribute to the Mongols, which helped to preserve some measure of order and stability in the region.
